title: Settlement Economy: production, consumption and trade of goods
about: The implementation plan for the design statement below, as components with features, the code each feature changes, and checks. tools/check_plan.py validates the plan, confirms every anchor still matches the mod source, and reports which features are done. Anchors are literal text in the mod checkout (GitLab main); 'added' checks are text the work will add.

statement.summary: Resources stop being map tokens a civilization has or lacks. They become goods in physical quantities, produced by each settlement from the land it works, its improvements, buildings, specialists and population, consumed in proportion to its size and way of life. Surpluses and shortages drive growth, contentment, industry, trade and war. Diplomacy moves from leasing a resource for gold per turn to real commerce: shipping goods, selling seeds and breeding stock, multi-part contracts.
principles: P1 Physical quantities: every good is counted in units that mean something (tonnes, bales, barrels, crates) and is conserved: made, moved, stored, used up or spoiled.

P2 Production comes from the whole settlement: worked tiles and their improvements, buildings, specialists and available labour. Land sets what is possible; people and capital set how much is realised.
P3 Consumption comes from population: needs per citizen rise with size and with era.
P4 Industry transforms goods at defined rates; the scarcest input limits the result.
P5 Military power has a material cost: units cost production and goods; armies in the field use supplies.
P6 Trade carries the goods themselves: goods, the means to produce them, money and treaties, in deals of any shape.
P7 The simulation lives in the DLL; XML holds the data; Python shows it.

decisions.question: Scale of units
decisions.choice: Real quantities in whole integers, each good in its own unit (tonnes, bales, barrels, crates), sized so no value can overflow; never shown as a fulfilment ratio.

decisions.question: Food
decisions.choice: Staple food is a good in tonnes. A city eats first and grows from its surplus; citizens starve only when stores are empty. Spoilage of food depends on the preservation technologies the owner lacks.

decisions.question: Need tiers
options: both: categories by era, quantities by development

decisions.question: Distribution
options: automatic within a trade network, limited by roads, rivers, ports and harbours
explicit shipments and routes managed by the player

decisions.question: Contracts and the trade screen
options: fit contracts into the executable's diplomacy screen (check first, feature TR.F7)
both: simple items in the diplomacy screen, contracts and packages in a Python screen

decisions.question: Order of work
options: settlements (goods, consumption), then industry, then trade

decisions.question: Icons
decisions.choice: Every good keeps its icon; new goods get their own font glyph, button and art define; no icon is missing or shared.

components.title: Groundwork
components.player_sees: Nothing changes in play. Every resource shows its own icon.

features.what: Goods catalogue: every resource record carries its unit, category (staple food, other food, fuel, raw material, intermediate, finished good, luxury, military supply), storage limit, spoilage rate per preservation technology, base value

Icons: the symbols after the resources are pinned so adding goods cannot shift them; the three shared glyphs (Diesel and Biofuel, Smart Medicine and Chemicals, Vulcanized and Synthetic Rubber) get their own; each new good gets a glyph in both font atlases, a button and an art define

checks.what: Civilopedia resource page and city screen show the right icon for every good; happy, health and other symbols unchanged

features.what: Goods accounts per settlement: stock, produced, consumed, received, sent, spoiled, per good, whole units, saved with the city
The bridge: a settlement supplied with a good holds the matching resource count in its trade network, next to a building's free resource
The economy pass: one call per player per turn, before its cities, in a fixed order (production, recipes, distribution, consumption, storage and spoilage)
Integer rules: per-settlement values in 32-bit with bounds from the records; sums and products in 64-bit; stocks capped by storage

checks.what: bounds written next to each new stock and flow; no product computed in 32-bit

components.title: Food and growth
components.player_sees: Food in tonnes on the city screen: produced, eaten, stored, lost to spoilage with the technology that would stop it. A city grows from its surplus and starves only when its stores are empty.

features.what: Staple food goods feed the city: citizens eat first, the surplus fills the food store that grows the city; the food yield on screen is a view of it

components.title: Consumption and needs
components.player_sees: Each settlement's needs in quantities (staple, dietary variety, fuel, clothing, comforts and luxuries) and what supplying them does to growth, health, contentment and output.

features.what: Needs per citizen by era and development: staple food; variety (dairy, meat, fruit, oil); fuel (wood, coal, oil); clothing (wool, cotton, linen); comforts and luxuries
Effects with diminishing returns: supplied needs add growth, health and contentment; shortfalls cause hunger, illness, unrest and lost production; the flat per-resource bonus goes
Breakdown texts name the goods behind each effect

components.title: Storage, spoilage and distribution
components.player_sees: Stocks limited by storage buildings; perishables decaying unless preserved; surpluses moving to shortages inside a trade network as far as roads, rivers, ports and harbours carry them; a blockade or a cut road changing what arrives.

features.what: Storage buildings (granary, warehouse) set each good's storage limit
Spoilage of every perishable good by the preservation technologies lacked
Distribution inside a trade network, limited by transport capacity of roads, rivers, ports and harbours; blockades cut sea links

components.title: Industry and units
components.player_sees: Buildings that convert inputs into outputs at set rates (2 iron ore and 1 coal make 2 steel); units that cost production plus goods; armies in the field drawing supplies.

features.what: Recipes with rates and capacities, run in dependency order; the scarcest input limits output
